title: Why robotics research rarely becomes practical products
why: Most experiments add little reusable knowledge; practical robots improved mainly through better electronics, batteries and manufacturing, not research.

title: Languages matter less than what you build
why: Reflective advice about boredom and focusing on users rather than languages; no concrete technique to learn.

title: Ops-friendly rules for deploying long-running services
why: Provide init scripts with start/stop/status, drop root privileges, use config files not XML, ship deb/rpm packaging, and fix bugs systems teams report.

title: Fake Hacker News front page prediction joke
why: A playful spoof of the HN front page ten years later; humor with no technical takeaway.

title: Enthusiasts' blind spots about data API pain
why: Commentary on a specific blog and thread; the useful point about Wikidata's query burden only makes sense in context.

title: Why answering became less rewarding on Stack Overflow
why: Contributor opinion on editing versus answering and closure policy; argumentative rather than explanatory.

title: Personal life advice from an old Marine
why: Opinionated life advice and political views with no technical or factual lesson to learn.

title: Why Bitcoin miners keep mining at a loss
why: Difficulty and hashrate track sunk costs and bets on future price, not current price, so much mining is unprofitable.

title: Personal memories of coal heating in rural England
why: Nostalgic first-hand anecdote about coal delivery and chores; interesting texture but no transferable lesson.

title: Comparing Flow and TypeScript issue tracker ratios
why: Issue-count comparison and impressions of maintainer responsiveness; the ratios are a weak signal of project quality.

title: Why frameworks exist: the raw DOM is hard for state
why: Raw DOM suits static pages but stateful UIs are hard; React composes components while frameworks add routing, state persistence and builds.

title: Solo developer's first app and feedback request
why: Personal origin story and request for feedback on a note app; no transferable technical insight.

title: Speculation that Apple's car effort is about CarPlay
why: Speculative prediction about CarPlay and phone-based car software with no evidence or technical depth.

title: Argument over whether ideas or execution matter
why: Defensive back-and-forth about founders' technical commitment; personal argument rather than explanation.

title: Repairability tension with hardware trust chains
why: Broad repair rules risk letting hostile parties replace security-critical parts like Touch ID; trusted hardware and repair goals genuinely conflict.

title: Older engineer's frustration with interview process
why: Personal job-search venting about LeetCode-style interviews; a sentiment, not an explanation a reader can learn from.

title: Past environmental doom predictions used as argument
why: Quotes failed 1970 predictions to argue against climate alarm; a rhetorical argument rather than substantive analysis.

title: Personal account of sleep problems after mono
why: Individual health anecdote about insomnia and CFS; no general lesson or verified treatment is offered.

title: Why starving cancer cells is hard in practice
why: Cancers reroute to anaerobic glycolysis and compete for blood supply, while replication-targeting drugs also hit skin, gut and immune cells.

title: Why soft-serve machines lock out and need service
why: Machines must complete nightly heat cycles and biweekly teardown for food safety; missed steps lock them out, often from operator error.

title: Algorithmic execution is not high-frequency trading
why: Algo trading means executing a large order over hours, like a pension buying AAPL; HFT is different, and critics are often misinformed.

title: Opinion on React and frontend state handling
why: Preference for React's API and async state patterns; personal taste rather than a transferable explanation.

title: Personal picks among low-fee US checking accounts
why: Product recommendations for specific banks from 2014; useful for one shopper but dated and not a general lesson.

title: Speculative essay on genetic differences by race
why: Politically charged speculation with hedged claims and no rigorous evidence; not a reliable learning source.

title: Essay defending entrepreneurs against social-good critics
why: Polemic against the expectation that startups benefit society; opinion rather than explanation.

title: Essay defending entrepreneurs against social-good critics
why: Polemic against the expectation that startups benefit society; opinion rather than explanation.

title: Google as a large company: context for critics
why: Counterpoint on Google's scale, transparency and processes from insider experience; mostly opinion defending the company.

title: Teen's letter to principal about outside work
why: Personal dispute letter about schoolwork and a business; no transferable lesson for technical readers.

title: Argument for IDEs over vim for large projects
why: Personal preference argument in an editor war; claims about productivity are unsupported and context-bound.

title: Letter to FDA opposing limits on DNA access
why: Political rant with speculation about insurer influence; advocacy letter rather than explanatory content.

title: Creating a local Windows 10 account without Microsoft
why: During setup, entering a wrong password for a Hotmail account reveals the option to create a local account instead.

title: Rant defending Google against Apple-centric critics
why: Emotional argument about openness and walled gardens; opinion with no concrete technical explanation.

title: Why youtube-dl's DMCA takedown legal theory is weak
why: Accessing with valid credentials is not circumvention under 1201(a)(2), as a court held, so the access-control claim looks shaky.

title: Choose-your-own-adventure ML reading list for engineers
why: Organized by prerequisites, beginner and intermediate texts; Metacademy and Ng's CS229 are good entry points for practitioners.

title: Consumers want sharing and playback, not encrypted sync
why: Observation that users value sharing features over encryption; product-market opinion rather than technical explanation.

title: Keyboard-only navigation on macOS is cumbersome
why: Reply disputing a keyboard claim with personal experience; a usability opinion that only makes sense against the quoted post.

title: Why parties converge and politics stays contentious
why: Parties act as brands that cut voter effort, and Hotelling convergence plus narrow majorities keeps US and Australian politics close and bitter.

title: Why Facebook is useful for keeping in touch
why: Personal argument that Facebook helps shy people stay connected; subjective experience rather than general knowledge.

title: Skeptical view of buying NFT versions of tweets
why: Opinion on whether NFTs confer ownership; argumentative commentary without technical explanation of the mechanism.

title: Why Reddit centralizes niche communities
why: Thoughtful observation that subreddits concentrate interest groups without tying identity, but mostly personal perspective on platform value.

title: Predicted side effects of streaming content quotas
why: Speculative policy critique about catalogs shrinking and piracy; plausible but argumentative with no evidence.

title: How one dinner outing flows through Google services
why: Gmail, Analytics, Calendar, Maps and voice search together log a simple dinner, including visits to sites not owned by Google.

title: Why extreme frugality early-retirement plans fail
why: Personal critique that lifestyle changes and job dissatisfaction break FIRE plans; opinion with anecdotal reasoning.

title: Humorous confession of an accidental self-checkout theft
why: Narrative humor about an accidental theft at self-checkout; entertaining but no lesson.

title: Why old dystopia archetypes fail to describe today
why: Argues tyranny and fascism labels no longer fit modern liberty threats; a thoughtful but unsupported opinion.

title: Satirical bedtime story of a startup bust
why: Humorous speculation about a 2015 bust cascading through startups; entertaining but not substantive analysis.

title: Doubts about unattended cameras for sports filming
why: Skeptical product critique of Soloshot-style cameras with practical concerns about theft and placement; mostly opinion.

title: Why self-driving hype ignores messy real-world roads
why: Vivid first-hand observations from Lima and poor suburbs; a fair point but mostly anecdote and skepticism.

title: Why Stack Overflow answers are freely licensed
why: Answers are a shared resource read by thousands, unlike Experts-Exchange's one-to-one model; CC licensing rejects the paywall approach.

title: Advice on raising consulting rates and networking
why: Personal career coaching on reputation, alumni networks and timing; sound but generic advice without concrete technique.

title: Defending Square's handling of a chargeback dispute
why: Explains that processors hold merchant funds for chargebacks, but the comment is a one-sided defense of a specific dispute.

title: Concern that Western society is losing traditional families
why: Culture-war opinion about gender roles and immigration; no evidence presented and not a technical lesson.

title: Why doctors' attitudes undermine hospital security
why: Doctors who resist passwords and MFA let security be overridden, and one phishing click by a doctor led to a costly breach.

title: Equity is not spendable compensation until exit
why: Options are worth nothing until an exit and cannot pay rent, so they motivate but cannot replace salary.

title: Hobby pricing driven by exclusivity and fashion
why: Enthusiast opinion that cheap builds perform similarly to expensive ones; subjective and anecdotal rather than explanatory.

title: Advice to walk away from a cofounder dispute
why: Personal advice to cut losses and avoid tying identity to an unfair split; sensible but situational, not technical.

title: Why angled solar arrays cannot beat optimal orientation
why: Independent panels' energy adds linearly, so each off-optimal angle yields less than one optimally oriented panel; no free energy.

title: Open questions about lab-leak hypotheses
why: Lists unanswered questions about COVID origins without new evidence; speculative and contested.

title: Defending California's integrated math curriculum
why: Argues the framework is integrated and applied rather than banning advanced math; a rebuttal in a heated debate, not a standalone lesson.

title: Personal IT career path through short contracts
why: Narrative of job-hopping through contracts and night shifts; relatable but no transferable technique beyond anecdote.

title: Mechanic's case for keeping older cars
why: Opinion that maintenance beats replacement and that safety tech responds to regulation; contested claims without data.

title: Worry about geographic pay cuts for tech workers
why: Speculative labor-market argument about salaries regressing to cheaper regions; opinion without data.

title: Machine learning as compressed memory of data
why: kNN stores data with no compression while neural networks compress it into weights, so models mostly reflect the data they were given.

title: Why small napkin machines cost far more per unit
why: Matching one industrial machine needs 175 small machines and about 700 workers, so labor and capital dominate while power costs stay minor.

title: Argument for effect size and statistical power
why: Agrees that tiny p-just-under-0.05 effects make weak foundations; a sound but general argument without new method.

title: Self-hosting email splits into three separate choices
why: Domain ownership, mailbox hosting and sending are separable; sending needs a stable IP with ongoing reputation monitoring, the hardest part.

title: Comparing US top jobs salaries by region
why: Compares salary figures for tech and health jobs in Bay Area cities; a loose data comparison with weak sourcing.

title: How a pre-blockchain digital notary chained hashes
why: Client hashes are batched into a Merkle tree whose root links into a super hash chain, so certificates prove a document existed at a timestamp.

title: Rebuttal on which Chinese COVID vaccines were effective
why: Lists several Chinese vaccines and cites real-world CoronaVac data; a reply within a heated thread, not a standalone lesson.

title: Missing computing education in 1990s UK schools
why: Personal account of office-focused computing courses and closed networking programs; no transferable technical lesson.

title: Moral critique of click farms and spam economics
why: Argument about desperation and extraction in gig economics; opinion with no technical content.

title: Hiring by short take-home and live code review
why: A one-hour take-home judged for tests and clarity, then an in-person session on the candidate's laptop, screens for real problem-solving over years of language experience.

title: Concern that nuclear needs decades of stable politics
why: Argues long-term reactor upkeep and decommissioning depend on stable governance; reasonable concern but mostly political opinion.

title: Argument against hiding https and www in URLs
why: Prefers positive security indicators over hiding information; a design opinion without concrete evidence or data.

title: Heat pumps cost more per watt saved than solar
why: Heat pump costs about 39 cents per saved watt versus about 7 cents for panels, before counting seasons and storage.

title: Plea to treat surveillance debate seriously
why: Calls for civility and defends the programs' purpose; a persuasive opinion with no technical content.

title: Index documentation by concept, not just function name
why: Reference manuals only help when you know the function name; concept-indexed docs let users discover functions by what they want to do.

title: Retail security harms honest customers
why: Argues anti-theft measures like alarms and tool locks create customer friction; a sensible opinion about retail design.

title: Defending Stack Overflow's question quality standards
why: Opinion that SO's answers beat search results and that question guidelines are fair; argumentative rather than instructive.

title: Encryption and identity are separate certificate problems
why: Domain-validated certs prove control of a domain, not trustworthiness; the bigger EV badges mostly reflect paid verification cost, not stronger encryption.

title: Parent's experience getting daughters into programming
why: Personal parenting anecdote about kids preferring phones and games; sentiment, not a transferable lesson.

title: Wish for a turnkey hosted infrastructure stack
why: Describes ops burden of running Kubernetes, logging and metrics for small teams; a product wish rather than a how-to.

title: Critique of US school board selection and success
why: Quotes Mark Twain and argues schools are inefficient; political opinion without data.

title: Argument that federal agencies exceed constitutional power
why: Constitutional opinion and political challenge about domain seizures; argumentative and contextual rather than explanatory.

title: Apple Silicon benchmark numbers were Rosetta emulation
why: The published numbers matched x86_64 binaries under Rosetta; the arm64 build returned invalid results, so verify architecture before trusting benchmarks.

title: Concerns about EU rules forcing interoperability
why: Argues hardware access and interoperability could undermine end-to-end encryption; a plausible but speculative policy opinion.

title: Why 3D games resist reusable blueprints
why: Game-design comparison of grid-based blueprints versus free 3D construction; thoughtful, but mostly opinion about two games.

title: Personal story of a weak hire and review fallout
why: Vent about a bad hire with code-review anecdotes; a cautionary story rather than a reusable technique.

title: Startup job listing for designers and engineers
why: Recruiting advertisement with marketing claims; no technical explanation.

title: Separate math input syntax from typesetting quality
why: Math quality comes from TeX's rendering rules, while input syntax and symbols are separate problems; Unicode and OpenType now bypass symbol lookup.

title: Why Brave New World is less dystopian than 1984
why: Argues Huxley's dystopia relies on implausible discontinuous changes while its realistic parts are not bad; a persuasive literary opinion.

title: Why institutions lost public trust
why: Opinion that overconfidence and deception eroded trust in science and media; a value judgment rather than a technical lesson.

title: Managing remote teams through deliverable accountability
why: Manager describes weekly syncs and public deliverable commitments that worked during lockdown; sound but anecdotal management advice.

title: Survival tips for an unplanned freefall
why: Surface area is the only way to slow down, relaxing muscles greatly improves survival odds, and aiming for trees, snow or skylights matters.

title: Personal memory of meeting a forum founder
why: Emotional tribute and personal anecdote about a planned lunch; no technical or general lesson.

title: Argument that police enforce law rather than mediate
why: Opinion about what calling police means at scale; reasonable framing but argumentative and not a technical explanation.

title: Discussion of classics teaching across countries
why: Personal question about Homer and Greek education in Sweden; discussion prompt without a concrete lesson.

title: Rebuttal of Paul Graham's essay on bosses
why: Critique of tone and absolutes in a startup essay, plus a personal view of working at a large organization.

title: Snobbish critique of AI art style
why: Subjective art criticism of DALL-E outputs; opinion and taste rather than explanation of how models work.

title: Godot's 2D and nested scenes beat Unity for pixel games
why: Unity needs workarounds for pixel-perfect 2D and lacks nested prefabs, while Godot uses pixel units and nested instances with few clicks.
